target.title: fix(sessions): prune stale entries independently of maxEntries gate
target.body:
"## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issue #103956: the `session.pruneAfter` configuration setting is silently ignored during normal gateway operation. Sessions older than the configured prune cutoff grow unbounded regardless of the `pruneAfter` duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

During load-time session store maintenance, stale-entry pruning (`pruneStaleEntries`) was gated by `Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries`. This meant age-based pruning only fired when the store exceeded its entry count limit. If a user had fewer sessions than `maxEntries` (default 500), no pruning ever happened — `pruneAfter` effectively became dead configuration.

The fix separates the pruning trigger from the entry-count gate, matching the established pattern in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` in `store-maintenance-operations.ts` which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally in enforce mode.

## User Impact

Users who configure `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` will now see sessions older than the configured duration automatically removed during load-time maintenance, regardless of how many sessions exist. The entry-count cap (`maxEntries`) continues to work exactly as before — it is still gated by `shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance` with its batched high-water-mark threshold (`maxEntries + 10%` slack).

## Evidence

### Root cause analysis

In `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`, the `pruneStaleEntries` call at load-time was gated by:
```typescript
if (maintenance.mode === "enforce" && Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries) {
```

This means age-based pruning (`pruneAfter`) could never fire independently of the entry-count gate. If the user had fewer sessions than `maxEntries` (default 500), no pruning happened — regardless of how old the sessions were.

### Reference implementation (already shipped, identical pattern)

The fix mirrors the established pattern in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` at [store-maintenance-operations.ts:214](src/config/sessions/store-maintenance-operations.ts#L214), which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally in enforce mode:

```typescript
// store-maintenance-operations.ts:214 — pruneStaleEntries runs unconditionally (shipped)
const pruned = pruneStaleEntries(params.operation.store, params.maintenance.pruneAfterMs, {
  onPruned: ({ entry }) => { rememberRemovedSessionFile(removedSessionFiles, entry); },
  preserveKeys: preserveSessionKeys,
});
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(params.operation.store).length;
const shouldRunCapMaintenance =
  params.forceMaintenance ||
  shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({ entryCount: countAfterPrune, maxEntries: params.maintenance.maxEntries });
const capped = shouldRunCapMaintenance ? capEntryCount(...) : 0;
```

```typescript
// store-load.ts (after fix — identical pattern)
pruned = pruneStaleEntries(store, maintenance.pruneAfterMs, {
  log: false,
  preserveKeys: preserveSessionKeys,
});
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(store).length;
capped = shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({
  entryCount: countAfterPrune,
  maxEntries: maintenance.maxEntries,
}) ? capEntryCount(store, maintenance.maxEntries, ...) : 0;
```

The only difference is that `store-maintenance-operations.ts` (write-time) passes `onPruned` for artifact cleanup, while `store-load.ts` (load-time) does not need artifact cleanup — this is expected because load-time maintenance only operates on the in-memory store before it's written.

### Existing test that proves the current behavior is intentional

`applyEnforcedMaintenance()` is already covered by 37 existing integration tests in `store.pruning.integration.test.ts` that verify pruning + capping work correctly in write-time maintenance. The fact that this function has always run `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally proves the constraining factor was the load-time gate, not the design intent.

### New regression test

Added `"explicit loadSessionStore maintenance prunes stale entries even when below maxEntries"` in `store.pruning.integration.test.ts`:

```
Test scenario:
  - 4 entries (well below default maxEntries=500)
  - 2 entries are 14–31 days old (exceeding pruneAfterMs=7 days)
  - 2 entries are recent (1 day and now)
  - Expected: stale entries pruned, recent entries survive
  - Expected: Object.keys(loaded).length === 2
```

**Result**: ✅ Passes

### Full test suite results

```bash
$ npx vitest run src/config/sessions/ --no-coverage
✓ 35 test files passed
✓ 495 tests passed
✓ 0 failures
```

### Lint and typecheck

```bash
$ npx oxlint --deny=warn --ignore-path=.oxlintignore \
    src/config/sessions/store-load.ts \
    src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts
✓ Clean, no warnings

$ pnpm check:test-types
✓ Passes
```

### Scope of change

```
$ git diff --stat upstream/main
 src/config/sessions/store-load.ts                  |  6 -----
 .../sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts     | 29 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 29 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
```

Only 2 files changed. No new infrastructure, no config surface changes, no new dependencies.

### Proof tier

L2 (vitest + fixture + targeted regression test). The fix is a pure structural correction that makes load-time maintenance consistent with the already-shipped write-time maintenance pattern in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()`.

### QA Smoke CI

The 2 QA Smoke CI failures are a fork-PR infrastructure limitation:
- Fork PRs run on `ubuntu-24.04` instead of `blacksmith-16vcpu-ubuntu-2404`
- The checkout step times out trying to fetch the full repository
- These jobs require `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1` which needs private QA infrastructure not available to fork PRs

All 63 other CI checks pass cleanly.

## Tests

```bash
# Full session test suite (495 passed across 35 files)
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/ --no-coverage

# Integration tests including new regression test (37 passed)
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts --no-coverage

# Unit tests (26 passed)
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts --no-coverage

# Lint (clean)
npx oxlint --deny=warn --ignore-path=.oxlintignore \
  src/config/sessions/store-load.ts \
  src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts

# Typecheck (passes)
pnpm check:test-types
```

## Risk

- **Behavior change**: Yes — stale pruning now works as documented during load-time maintenance
- **Config change**: No
- **Data loss risk**: Low — pruning uses the same `pruneAfterMs` threshold already configured; no new deletion path. The capping step remains gated by `shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance` with its batched high-water-mark threshold (`maxEntries + 10%` slack).
- **Performance impact**: Low — `pruneStaleEntries` is O(n) on session count and was already called during every load-time maintenance pass when over the entry limit
- **Compatibility risk**: The change makes load-time maintenance consistent with the already-shipped write-time maintenance in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()`. Active session and pointer keys are preserved via `collectSessionMaintenancePreserveKeysForStore()`.

## Current Review State

Changes since initial submission:
1. ✅ Removed 3 committed process artifacts (pr-103956-body.md, spec-103956.md, session-log-103956.md)
2. ✅ Added targeted regression test proving the fix works for the below-maxEntries scenario
3. ✅ Fixed oxlint `no-implicit-coercion` warning
4. ✅ Rebased on latest main (conflict resolved — upstream renamed `collectSessionMaintenancePreserveKeys` → `collectSessionMaintenancePreserveKeysForStore`)
5. ✅ All 495 session tests pass, lint clean, typecheck clean

Ready for re-review.
"

target.title: fix(agents): respect provider default thinking level over global thinkingDefault
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron agentTurn jobs using Ollama models produce empty responses when `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is configured, because the global default unconditionally overrides the provider's own default of `"off"`.

- **Problem**: `resolveThinkingDefault()` checks `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` before the provider-specific default, so when a user has `thinkingDefault: "low"` (common for Claude), Ollama receives a non-`"off"` thinking level → `think: true` in the Ollama API → model consumes 100% of output tokens on reasoning → empty `content` → "Agent couldn't generate a response"
- **Solution**: Resolve the provider-specific default first, then only apply the global `thinkingDefault` when the provider does not explicitly default to `"off"`
- **What changed**: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts` (reorder evaluation in `resolveThinkingDefault()`), new test file `src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts`
- **What did NOT change**: Per-model `params.thinking` priority, Claude hardcoded special cases, the Ollama provider plugin, or any behavior for providers without an explicit default

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #104212

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` is set to enable thinking for the primary model (usually Claude), the global default unconditionally overrides every provider's own default thinking level. For Ollama, which explicitly defaults to `"off"` in `extensions/ollama/provider-policy-api.ts`, this forces `think: true` in the Ollama API request, causing models like Qwen3.5-4B to consume all output tokens on reasoning and produce zero visible content.

The same Ollama workflow works correctly when no global `thinkingDefault` is set, or when `params.thinking` is explicitly configured per model.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` must not override provider-specific defaults that are `"off"`
- Real environment tested: Ubuntu Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/ollama-respect-default-thinking-104212`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm tsgo:core      # type check
npx oxfmt --check src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # format check
npx oxlint --deny-warnings src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts  # lint check
pnpm test src/agents/model-thinking-default.test.ts --run  # unit tests
pnpm check:import-cycles  # cycle check
```

- Evidence after fix (real runtime invocation via `resolveThinkingDefault()`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import { resolveThinkingDefault } from './src/agents/model-thinking-default.js'; ..."

Real Behavior Evidence — PR #104248 / Fixes #104212
Environment: Node v22.19.0, linux
========================================
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=low                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=adaptive                result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + global thinkingDefault=off                     result=off (expected off)
PASS | No global default                                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=adaptive                     result=adaptive (expected adaptive)
PASS | Claude Sonnet 4.6 + global=low                          result=low (expected low)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.7 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Claude Opus 4.8 + global=adaptive                       result=off (expected off)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=low + global=adaptive         result=low (expected low)
PASS | Ollama + per-model params=off + global=low              result=off (expected off)
========================================
10 passed, 0 failed
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  2. Ollama + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (provider default wins)
  3. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "low"` → `"low"` (per-model override works)
  4. Ollama + per-model `params.thinking: "off"` → `"off"` (per-model override works)
  5. Unknown provider + global `thinkingDefault: "low"` → `"low"` (no provider default, global applies)
  6. Claude Opus 4.7 + global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` → `"off"` (hardcoded special case preserved)
  7. No global default → returns provider default

- What was not tested: Real Ollama end-to-end with actual model inference (requires local Ollama instance with a thinking-capable model). The fix is in a pure function whose behavior is fully covered by real runtime invocation with 10/10 scenarios passing.
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission change
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All thinking levels (`off`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`adaptive`/etc.) handled by existing checks; the fix only reorders them
  - ✅ Path coverage: Single change in shared `resolveThinkingDefault()` covers cron, embedded runner (session), and subagent paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state to clean up

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`, `resolveThinkingDefault()` checked `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` (lines 71-73) **before** `resolveThinkingDefaultForModel()` (lines 101-106), so the global config default unconditionally overrode the provider-specific default from plugin policy or catalog metadata.

Introduced by: Peter Steinberger (`steipete`) in commit `d5eec80e340` — the initial implementation of `resolveThinkingDefault()`.

## Regression Test Plan

All 9 new unit tests pass on every run. Existing `thinking-runtime.test.ts` (8 tests) continues to pass — no behavioral change for Claude models or unconfigured providers.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Ollama users who have `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` set will no longer see forced thinking mode in cron agentTurn jobs. The Ollama model will run with its default behavior (thinking off) unless explicitly configured per-model via `agents.defaults.models[].params.thinking`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All code paths through `resolveThinkingDefault()` — per-model override, Claude special cases, Ollama default with global config, unknown provider with global config, no global config
- Edge cases checked: Global `thinkingDefault: "off"` with provider that also defaults to "off" (result is "off" either way); global `thinkingDefault: "adaptive"` for unknown provider with reasoning model
- What you did NOT verify: Real Ollama E2E without a local Ollama instance

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — the only behavioral change is that providers with `defaultLevel: "off"` are no longer overridden by the global default, which is a bug fix
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared layer (`resolveThinkingDefault()`) is the correct boundary because all code paths (cron, session, subagent) depend on it. A cron-only fix would have been ineffective because the embedded runner independently resolves defaults.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Removing the `resolveThinkingDefault()` call from the cron path only — rejected because the embedded runner (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts:291-314`) independently resolves defaults via the same function, so the bug would reappear for non-cron paths

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes

target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Web-search credential presence detection mixed ordinary provider options with real credentials, and the later manifest-based credential scan could still treat policy-blocked web-search plugins as usable. That left the security/audit heuristic vulnerable to both false positives from disabled/denylisted/not-allowed plugins and false negatives around explicitly selected keyless providers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detector now only counts direct or scoped `apiKey` values under `tools.web.search`, applies consistent SecretRef/env semantics, checks plugin `webSearch` credentials including `baseUrl`, and treats manifest-declared bundled providers with `requiresCredential: false` as configured when explicitly selected.

The manifest pass now also carries one policy scope through the candidate checks: `plugins.enabled === false`, `plugins.allow`, `plugins.deny`, and per-entry `enabled: false` remove blocked plugin/provider candidates before keyless, env-var, and raw config credentials can count. Raw plugin-entry credentials are not narrowed to the bundled origin, so configured external web-search plugins still count unless the plugin policy blocks them.

## User Impact

Security/audit and setup paths get fewer false positives from non-credential search options and policy-blocked web-search plugins, while preserving configured external plugin credentials and explicitly selected keyless web-search providers. No live provider key is needed for the regression proof.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` (25 tests)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts`

## Proof

target.title: fix(agents): distinguish z.ai code 1305 content rejection from generic overload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with code 1305 deterministically when the system prompt contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". The current error classifier treats all 1305 responses as generic overload, showing "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" to users — which is misleading for the content-rejection case.

**Solution**: Add a `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` pattern to detect `{"code":1305,...}` or `{"code":"1305",...}` (quoted or unquoted) in the raw error message and surface a more specific diagnostic before falling back to the generic overload message.

**What changed**: 
- `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: Updated `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` regex constant to match both `"code":1305` (unquoted number) and `"code":"1305"` (quoted string) JSON values; new check in `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` that runs before `isOverloadedErrorMessage` and returns a more precise message for z.ai 1305 errors
- `failover-matches.test.ts`, `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`: Updated tests to expect the new diagnostic message; added test for the canonical z.ai payload format `{"error":{"code":"1305",...}}`

**What did NOT change**:
- The `rate_limit` failover classification is preserved — backoff and fallback continue working
- Non-1305 overload errors return the original "overloaded" message unchanged
- Zhipu GLM `[1305]` format is not affected (doesn't match the JSON key pattern)

**Fixes**: #103529

## What Problem This Solves

Users onboarding a valid z.ai Coding Plan key successfully, but every chat turn fails with a misleading "overloaded" error. The real cause — the system prompt signature line triggering a provider-side content filter — is invisible. Users waste time checking quota, retrying, or switching API keys when the issue is the system prompt content.

## Root Cause

z.ai's Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with `{"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}}` when the system message contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". This behavior is a **deterministic function of the system prompt content**, not a transient overload. Removing or altering that one line produces a 200 response.

The error classifier in `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` matched the "overloaded" keyword in the response body and returned the generic overload message, which is incorrect for this scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Error message for z.ai code 1305 now correctly mentions possible content rejection

**Real environment tested**: Node 24, macOS, tsx 4.19, vitest 4.1.9

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
```terminal
node --import tsx zai-1305-demo.ts
```
The script directly calls the actual exported function `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` (L2 real-module execution) with both the canonical z.ai payload and other error scenarios.

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal
=== z.ai 1305 Content Rejection Diagnostic — L2 Behavior Proof ===

--- Case 1: Canonical z.ai payload (quoted string code, nested error object) ---
Input: {"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305 ("overloaded"). This may indicate system prompt content triggered a provider filter rather than a transient overload — try a different model or system prompt, or retry.

--- Case 2: Unquoted numeric code value (backward compatible) ---
Input: {"code":1305,"message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305 ("overloaded"). This may indicate system prompt content triggered a provider filter rather than a transient overload — try a different model or system prompt, or retry.

--- Case 3: HTTP status prefix + unquoted code ---
Input: 429 status code (exceeded limit)
{"code":1305,"message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305 ("overloaded"). This may indicate system prompt content triggered a provider filter rather than a transient overload — try a different model or system prompt, or retry.

--- Case 4: Generic overload (should return generic message) ---
Input: {"error":{"message":"Overloaded"}}
Output: The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment.

--- Case 5: Rate limit with actionable retry details ---
Input: 429 rate limit: service overloaded, try again in 30 seconds
Output: ⚠️ rate limit: service overloaded, try again in 30 seconds
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` now returns "⚠️ Provider returned code 1305...possible content rejection" instead of "The AI service is temporarily overloaded." — for both `"code":1305` and `"code":"1305"` payload formats, including the canonical `{"error":{"code":"1305",...}}` nesting. Non-1305 overloads and rate-limit messages fall through to their original behavior.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end with a real z.ai API key (L3 full gateway run). The original issue (#103529) provides curl-level reproduction. L2 real-module execution (npx tsx directly calling the exported function) covers all payload formats the formatter is designed to handle. A full gateway run would additionally exercise the end-to-end error propagation pipeline.

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)
5. The real model transport (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:231`) already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${version}`, which is why actual chat works once the endpoint is configured

**Affected scope**:
- **Affected**: All z.ai Coding Plan onboarding flows (new users, re-auth, config migration)
- **Not affected**: z.ai standard and CN endpoints (these happen to not require UA, or the standard endpoint is tried first and happens to succeed with certain key types)
- **Not affected**: Existing users with manually configured baseUrl
- **Version**: Present since the `detectZaiEndpoint` feature was introduced; became user-visible when z.ai's edge started enforcing the UA check

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: z.ai endpoint auto-detection probe requests now include a User-Agent header, allowing z.ai's edge to accept them instead of returning HTTP 429.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 (build 17763), Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2, vitest 4.1.8

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Navigate to the fix worktree and run the full detect test suite:

```bash
cd openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100
npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 tests pass. The new test (`includes user-agent header in probe requests`) creates a mock fetch that captures request headers, invokes `detectZaiEndpoint`, and asserts that `capturedHeaders["user-agent"]` matches the pattern `/^openclaw\//`. This confirms the UA header is present in every probe request after the fix.

**What was not tested**: Live z.ai Coding Plan endpoint detection (requires valid z.ai provider credentials, not available from this contributor's environment). The original issue reporter's before/after live output (Issue #98100 body) confirms that adding any User-Agent header resolves the 429 from z.ai's edge. The code change is purely additive (one HTTP header), and the unit tests validate the header is correctly included in all probe requests.

## Summary

**Problem**: The `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` regex patterns in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` recognized bare thinking tags and `antml:` namespaced tags but not `mm:` namespaced MiniMax reasoning tags. When a MiniMax model produced reasoning output behind a Matrix channel, raw `<mm:think>` / `<mm:thought>` tags leaked through to end users instead of being suppressed.

**Solution**: Add `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix alternative to the `think(?:ing)?|thought` group in both regex constants. This matches the fix applied to 6 other channel/processing modules in prior PRs (#93767, #93806, #93820).

**What changed**: Two regex constants in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` (lines 8-11). The alternatives group was restructured to add `mm:` namespace prefix support.

```typescript
// Before (missing mm: namespace):
/(?:think(?:ing)?|thought|antthinking)/

// After (all known namespace prefixes):
/(?:(?:antml:|mm:)?(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)|antthinking)/
```

**What did NOT change**: The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` function logic, `deliverMatrixReplies()` public API, message sending, media handling, thread/reply routing. All previously-matched tag patterns continue to work identically — the change is strictly additive.

Fixes #99412

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #93767 (core reasoning-tags), #93806 (silent-reply/streaming), #93820 (iMessage)
- **In scope**: Matrix monitor `replies.ts` regex constants
- **Out of scope**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration (requires live MiniMax API key)

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: MiniMax model (or Fireworks-provider inlining `mm:` prefixed reasoning) produces reasoning via Matrix channel. The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` regex lacked `mm:` namespace prefix, so reasoning tags passed through as visible text.

**Root cause**: Each channel module maintains its own local copy of thinking-tag regex patterns. When `mm:` support was added to the core `reasoning-tags.ts` (#93767), this matrix module was missed. This is the 4th and final instance of this synchronization gap.

## Real behavior proof

**What was not tested**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration with a live MiniMax model producing `mm:think` tags. This would require a running Matrix server + MiniMax API key. target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users or jobs with exact embedded-run tool allowlists could lose the requested tool when its hand-maintained factory classification had drifted. `transcripts` was routed away from its core factory, while plugin-owned `canvas` was routed away from plugin construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core tool identity and factory family now live in one lightweight typed catalog. The attempt planner classifies each normalized allowlist once, while plugin, MCP, and LSP discovery remain on their existing runtime paths.

## User Impact

Exact allowlists now expose `transcripts` and `canvas` through their actual owners. Future core-tool additions have catalog-to-factory regression coverage instead of requiring parallel name maps to remain synchronized manually.

## Evidence

- Source-built ephemeral Gateway E2E at exact head `fe131d2951de20ff0e8488f4b8bc552e42996b16` under Node 24: two ordinary CLI-created one-shot isolated cron jobs completed with status `ok`; captured model requests advertised exactly `transcripts` for `toolsAllow: ["transcripts"]` and exactly `canvas` for `toolsAllow: ["canvas"]`. target.title: fix(agents): keep scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where SCP stderr tail truncation can produce invalid Unicode when sandbox filenames contain emoji or other supplementary-plane characters.

`appendScpStderrTail()` caps raw `child.stderr` output with `combined.slice(-maxChars)` before the text is surfaced in `throw new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`)`. SCP stderr is unfiltered (unlike treemap label sanitization), so paths like `📊report.csv` can land on a UTF-16 surrogate boundary and leave a lone high surrogate in operator/agent-visible errors.

**Concrete example:** `appendScpStderrTail("prefix", "🤖tail", 5)` with the old slice could keep `U+D83D` without its low half; the thrown error then carries malformed Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw tail slice with `sliceUtf16Safe(combined, Math.max(0, combined.length - maxChars))` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the established tail-truncation pattern in `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts` (#103757) and `src/node-host/invoke.ts`. Ring-buffer size and SCP behavior are unchanged; only the truncation boundary is surrogate-safe.

## User Impact

**Before:** SCP failures for media staging can surface replacement glyphs or invalid Unicode in agent/operator error text when stderr mentions emoji filenames near the tail cap.

**After:** SCP stderr tails remain well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts` — `appendScpStderrTail` uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for the tail cap
- `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` — shared surrogate backoff helper
- Helper regression: `src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts`
- Caller-path regression: `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts` (`testing.scpFile` mocked `spawn` stderr bisect case)
- Live subprocess proof: production `testing.scpFile` and `stageSandboxMedia` exercised with the real `/usr/bin/scp` binary (no `spawn` mock)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** SCP stderr tail truncation no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when an emoji filename crosses the tail cap before the error is thrown to the agent/operator.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `stageSandboxMedia` remote attachment staging → `scpFile` spawns `scp` → `child.stderr` chunks → `appendScpStderrTail` ring buffer → `finish(new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`))` on non-zero exit.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real OpenSSH `scp` subprocess via production `testing.scpFile`, plus `stageSandboxMedia` remote-cache path with emoji attachment filename and captured runtime log line.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`; provider/channel constraints N/A because this is sandbox media staging stderr handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22, branch `fix/scp-stderr-tail-utf16` @ `e8222a145cc`, real `/usr/bin/scp` against `git@github.com` (public host; no operator credentials printed).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ pnpm install   # once, in repo root with devDependencies
$ pnpm exec tsx -e "
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { testing } from './src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts';
(async () => {
  const tmp = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'scp-live-proof-'));
  try {
    await testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', path.join(tmp, 'download'));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
  } finally {
    await fs.rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
})();
"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx …testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', …)
scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed

$ OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 node --import tsx -e "
…stageSandboxMedia({ remoteMediaMode: 'cache', ctx.MediaRemoteHost: 'git@github.com', MediaPath: '/Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg', … })
"
Failed to stage inbound media path /Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg: Error: scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
unpaired_surrogates=false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose

Test Files  2 passed (2)
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
